description: Adult C. elegans hermaphrodites used as the experimental subject population in which daf-2 mutations were studied for effects on lifespan and development. They are the organismal context for the observed longevity phenotype and dauer-related regulation.

The baseline comparison population of normal C. elegans used as the reference for lifespan and developmental phenotypes. It serves as the control condition against which mutant longevity is contrasted.

Genetic perturbations in daf-2 that alter lifespan and developmental regulation in C. elegans. In the text, these mutations are the initiating biological change associated with extended lifespan and dauer formation effects.

A second gene required for the lifespan extension caused by daf-2 mutations. It functions as a key molecular determinant in the longevity pathway and also participates in regulation of dauer formation.

A developmentally arrested larval form of C. elegans that is induced by crowding and starvation and is described as very long-lived. It represents a developmental and longevity-related endpoint in the study.
The arrested developmental state characteristic of the dauer larva. It captures the process of developmental arrest that is linked to dauer formation and longevity.
An environmental condition that induces dauer larva formation in C. elegans. It provides the contextual trigger for the developmental response described in the abstract.
A nutritional environmental condition that induces dauer larva formation in C. elegans. It is part of the context in which the long-lived dauer state is generated.
A regulated biological mechanism proposed to explain the increased longevity observed in daf-2 mutants and in dauer larvae. It is presented as separable from other aspects of dauer formation.
The extended lifespan phenotype observed in daf-2 mutants and dauer larvae. It is the central outcome of interest in the study.

A nematode model organism used here as the biological subject for studying insulin-like peptide biology, signaling, and conserved endocrine mechanisms. It serves as an experimental system for understanding peptide structure, regulation, and functional roles in development and longevity.

A family of hormone-like molecular signals involved in regulating metabolism, growth, and development. In this text they are the central molecular features under review, including their structures, processing, tissue localization, regulation, and signaling roles in C. elegans.

The set of genes encoded in the C. elegans genome that produce insulin-like peptides. This gene family is notable for its large size and is relevant to the diversity and regulation of insulin-like signaling in the organism.
The single C. elegans insulin-like peptide receptor. It is the key receptor mediating insulin-like peptide signaling and is central to the IIS pathway in worms.

entity_name: INSULIN AND INSULIN-LIKE GROWTH FACTOR SIGNALING (IIS) PATHWAY
description: An evolutionarily conserved signaling pathway that transduces insulin-like peptide signals to regulate growth, metabolism, development, and longevity. In this text it is highlighted as a conserved mechanism from worms to humans.
A core physiological process regulated by insulin-like peptides, involving energy balance and nutrient utilization. It is one of the major functional outputs discussed in the review.

A biological process influenced by insulin-like peptide signaling, including organismal and developmental growth control. It is explicitly listed as a major function of insulin-like peptides in animals and C. elegans.
A biological process regulated by insulin-like peptides, encompassing organismal developmental progression. The text emphasizes its role in C. elegans and in conserved IIS biology.

A specialized developmental process in the reproductive lineage that is influenced by insulin-like peptide signaling in C. elegans. It is one of the example contexts for peptide function mentioned in the abstract.
A neurobiological process reported as an example of insulin-like peptide signaling effects in C. elegans. It indicates that these peptides have roles beyond metabolism and development.
An organism-level lifespan-related endpoint influenced by insulin-like peptide signaling in C. elegans. It is presented as a functional outcome of IIS pathway activity.

A descriptive analytical focus used to determine where insulin-like peptides are expressed or act within tissues. In the review, it is part of the literature overview of peptide biology and distribution.
The control of insulin-like peptide expression, processing, and signaling activity. The abstract notes regulation as a major topic in understanding peptide function in C. elegans.
Structural characteristics of insulin-like peptides that are reviewed in the paper. These features are relevant to peptide function, receptor interaction, and signaling properties.
The maturation and modification of insulin-like peptides into functional forms. It is discussed as part of the literature on peptide biology in C. elegans.

A functional property of some C. elegans insulin-like peptides whereby they oppose receptor signaling rather than activate it. This distinguishes them from human insulin-like peptides, which are described as agonists.
The nematode model organism discussed in the review; it is the biological subject in which neuropeptide genes, receptors, and behavioral phenotypes are analyzed.
A gene set in C. elegans encoding neuropeptide precursors; the text describes their number, expression patterns, and experimental inactivation or overexpression.
Bioactive signaling peptides derived from precursor molecules and implicated in modulation of behavior in C. elegans; includes insulin-like, FMRFamide-related, and other peptide classes.
Precursor proteins that are post-translationally processed to generate active neuropeptides; they may contain one or multiple peptide copies or distinct peptides.
The maturation process by which neuropeptide precursors are cleaved and modified to yield active peptides.
A major class of C. elegans neuropeptides encoded by 40 genes, representing one of the identified peptide families in the genome.
A major class of C. elegans neuropeptides encoded by 31 genes, representing a distinct peptide family involved in signaling.
The remaining identified neuropeptide class in C. elegans, encoded by 42 genes and distinct from insulin-like and FMRFamide-related peptides.
The anatomical setting in which neuropeptide genes are extensively expressed, including sensory, motor, and interneurons.
A neuronal tissue context where neuropeptide genes are expressed, contributing to sensory signaling and behavioral modulation.
A neuronal tissue context where neuropeptide genes are expressed, relevant to locomotor control.
A neuronal tissue context where neuropeptide genes are expressed, supporting integration of neural signals and behavior.
A non-neuronal tissue in which some neuropeptide genes are expressed, indicating broader tissue distribution beyond the nervous system.
A non-neuronal tissue where some neuropeptide genes are expressed, suggesting peripheral roles for neuropeptide signaling.
A non-neuronal tissue in which some neuropeptide genes are expressed, indicating tissue-specific expression outside the nervous system.
Molecular targets to which neuropeptides bind; they are being identified and examined to understand neuropeptide signaling and behavioral effects.
A behavioral endpoint reported as defective in knockout animals lacking certain neuropeptide genes.
A developmental/behavioral endpoint in C. elegans reported to be altered in neuropeptide gene knockout animals.
A reproductive behavioral endpoint reported as defective in animals with inactivated neuropeptide genes.
A behavioral response endpoint reported as altered in knockout animals analyzed for neuropeptide function.
A complex behavioral endpoint reported as defective in animals lacking certain neuropeptide genes.
The broad functional endpoint modulated by neuropeptides in C. elegans, encompassing multiple specific behavioral phenotypes.
C. elegans animals in which neuropeptide genes have been inactivated; used to assess the functional consequences of loss of neuropeptide signaling.
Experimental gene-loss status applied to neuropeptide genes in knockout animals to study functional effects on behavior.
Experimental gene-upregulation status applied to neuropeptide genes to assess effects on C. elegans behavior.

The nematode model organism discussed as the biological subject for which intermediary metabolism, developmental metabolic changes, stress responses, and lifespan-associated metabolic alterations are described.
The set of core metabolic pathways and enzyme-mediated reactions in C. elegans that support energy production, biosynthesis, and adaptation across development and environmental stress.
The developmental progression of the worm during which metabolic patterns and activity change, indicating stage-dependent regulation of metabolism.
The age-associated biological process in which metabolic patterns and activity change in C. elegans, reflecting altered physiology over time.
An unfavorable external environmental stressor mentioned as a condition that C. elegans can respond to, affecting metabolic state and activity.
A nutrient-limitation environmental condition that acts as an unfavorable external factor influencing metabolic responses in C. elegans.
A low-oxygen environmental condition that alters metabolic patterns in C. elegans and promotes microaerobic metabolic adaptation.
A developmental arrest state in C. elegans characterized by enhanced stress resistance, hypometabolism, and altered pathway usage that supports survival under adverse conditions.
A damaging stress response state against which dauer diapause is described as having enhanced resistance, indicating improved stress tolerance.
Metabolic pathways favored under low-oxygen conditions during dauer diapause, reflecting adaptation to reduced oxygen availability.
Metabolic pathways that replenish citric acid cycle intermediates and are increased in importance during dauer diapause.
A reduced metabolic state associated with dauer diapause, supporting prolonged survival under unfavorable conditions.
A metabolic pathway whose increased importance is noted during dauer diapause, contributing to altered energy metabolism under low-oxygen conditions.
Metabolic pathways that become more important during dauer diapause and support alternative carbon utilization and survival.
The activity of the citric acid cycle, described as being repressed during dauer diapause, indicating a shift away from canonical aerobic metabolism.
The survival outcome promoted by metabolic alterations during dauer larva state, representing an adaptive fitness endpoint.
The larval stage of C. elegans in dauer diapause, serving as the subject population whose survival is prolonged by metabolic remodeling.
A signaling axis referenced in relation to extended lifespan and associated metabolic changes in C. elegans mutants.
Mutant C. elegans strains with mitochondrial alterations that exhibit extended lifespan and some dauer-like metabolic changes.
An increased longevity phenotype observed in insulin/IGF-1 and several mitochondrial mutants, linked to altered metabolic states.
The dietary and metabolic needs of C. elegans discussed as part of intermediary metabolism and organismal energy balance.
The biological process of storing energy reserves in C. elegans, relevant to metabolic state and survival under stress.
Metabolic byproducts generated by C. elegans, mentioned as part of the overview of intermediary metabolism and organismal physiology.

A forkhead box transcription factor class O (FoxO) homolog in Caenorhabditis elegans that integrates upstream signaling to regulate transcriptional programs involved in aging, development, stress responses, metabolism, and immunity.

The forkhead box transcription factor class O family referenced as the homologous functional class of DAF-16, central to stress resistance, metabolic regulation, and longevity-associated transcriptional control.
The nematode model organism in which DAF-16 function and insulin/IGF-1 signaling-dependent metabolic remodeling are described.
A conserved signaling pathway that acts as the major upstream regulator of DAF-16 activity and whose reduction promotes lifespan extension and dauer-associated metabolic remodeling.
An aging-related outcome observed when IIS is reduced, reported across worms, flies, mice, and humans in the context of conserved longevity regulation.
Caenorhabditis elegans mutant worms with reduced IIS signaling, used as the genetic context in which DAF-16-dependent dauer survival and metabolic changes are described.
A heterochronic survival program activated during adulthood in daf-2 mutants under reduced IIS, associated with stress resistance and metabolic adaptation.
A protective stress-response process elevated as part of the dauer survival program, contributing to resistance against oxidative damage.

entity_name: METABOLIC SHIFT TOWARD ACCUMULATION OF CARBOHYDRATES
description: A metabolic remodeling process in which carbohydrate stores increase, including trehalose and glycogen accumulation, as part of the dauer survival program.
A nonreducing disaccharide that accumulates during the metabolic shift in daf-2 mutants and is implicated in supporting longevity.
A carbohydrate storage molecule that accumulates during IIS reduction and dauer-associated metabolic remodeling.
Lipid storage molecules that accumulate during the metabolic shift associated with dauer survival and reduced IIS.
A metabolic pathway activated during the dauer survival program that may enable conversion of fat to carbohydrate.
A proposed metabolic function enabled by activation of the glyoxylate shunt, supporting energy reallocation during dauer survival.
Trehalose produced by the organism itself, described as partially supporting the longevity of daf-2 mutants.
A comparative vertebrate group noted as unable to synthesize trehalose, highlighting species differences in downstream IIS mechanisms.
A biological process regulated by DAF-16 transcriptional activity and influenced by IIS reduction in the context of longevity control.
A biological process influenced by DAF-16-mediated transcriptional regulation downstream of upstream signaling pathways.
A broad biological response category regulated by DAF-16, including protective programs such as antioxidant defense.
A biological process controlled by DAF-16 that undergoes remodeling under reduced IIS, including carbohydrate and lipid accumulation.
A biological process regulated by DAF-16 through transcriptional changes in genes involved in host defense.

The nematode model organism discussed as the biological subject in which insulin/IGF-1 signaling, DAF-16/FOXO regulation, and lifespan control are studied. It serves as the experimental population for the pathway relationships described in the abstract.

A conserved signaling cascade in C. elegans that regulates multiple physiological processes including lifespan, fat storage, dauer diapause, reproduction, and stress response. It acts upstream of DAF-16 and is central to the paper's mechanistic focus.
The longevity phenotype regulated by insulin/IGF-1 signaling and DAF-16. It is the primary outcome emphasized in the abstract and is influenced by multiple upstream pathways.
A physiological endpoint controlled by the insulin/IGF-1 signaling pathway in C. elegans. It is one of several downstream biological outcomes mentioned in the abstract.
A developmental arrest state in C. elegans regulated by insulin/IGF-1 signaling. It represents a stress-adaptive biological process linked to pathway control.
A core biological process in C. elegans that is regulated by insulin/IGF-1 signaling and integrated with lifespan control through DAF-16-related signaling.
A protective cellular/organismal response process influenced by insulin/IGF-1 signaling and downstream DAF-16 activity. It is one of the major processes controlled by the pathway.
The insulin/IGF-1 receptor in C. elegans that initiates signaling through the PI 3-kinase/AKT pathway. It functions upstream of DAF-16 and is a key molecular component of the pathway.

A conserved intracellular signaling pathway downstream of DAF-2 that transmits insulin/IGF-1 signals and ultimately down-regulates DAF-16. It is a mechanistic bridge between receptor activation and transcriptional control.

A forkhead transcription factor (FOXO) in C. elegans that integrates signals from multiple pathways and regulates downstream target genes. It is the central molecular regulator of lifespan and other processes described in the abstract.
The transcription factor family designation for DAF-16, indicating its conserved FOXO identity and role in transcriptional regulation of downstream genes.
A reproductive-system-derived signaling source that provides input to DAF-16 and regulates lifespan in C. elegans. It represents one of the additional pathways influencing DAF-16 activity.
A signaling pathway that regulates lifespan in C. elegans by modulating nuclear translocation of DAF-16. It is an upstream pathway contributing to DAF-16 control.

entity_name: NUCLEAR TRANSLOCATION OF FORKHEAD TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR/DAF-16
description: The movement of DAF-16 into the nucleus, a regulatory process modulated by the JNK pathway and important for DAF-16-dependent transcriptional activity and lifespan regulation.
Genes regulated by DAF-16 that mediate its downstream effects on diverse biological processes, including lifespan control. They represent the transcriptional output of DAF-16 signaling.

The nematode model organism studied in this paper. It serves as the experimental subject for analyzing insulin signaling, dauer entry, and germ line-somatic gonad interactions during developmental decision-making.

The developmental stage of C. elegans examined for plasticity in response to environmental conditions. Larvae are the population that either proceeds through reproductive development or enters dauer diapause depending on signaling and context.

The first larval stage of C. elegans that can enter an alternative developmental pathway under adverse conditions. This stage is specifically described as the point at which dauer-associated developmental diversion begins.

A specialized arrested developmental form of C. elegans that survives in suspended development and can later recover when conditions improve. It represents the dauer diapause state central to the study.

A specific tissue compartment in C. elegans identified as the cellular focus where low insulin signaling is sufficient to promote dauer entry. It functions as an endocrine-like regulatory site in the developmental decision.
Cells that give rise to the germ line and are experimentally ablated in the study. Their presence is required for the full dauer-promoting effect when DAF-2 is depleted in the somatic gonad.

A canonical signaling pathway controlling the developmental choice between reproductive growth and dauer entry in C. elegans. It includes DAF-2/insulin receptor, AKT, and DAF-16/FoxO as major components.
The developmental transition into dauer diapause. It is the key biological decision regulated by insulin signaling activity in the somatic gonad and influenced by germ line interactions.
The prolonged arrested developmental state entered by C. elegans under adverse conditions. It is characterized by suspended development, quiescent precursor cells, and enhanced survival.
The normal developmental trajectory leading from larval stages to reproductive adulthood under favorable conditions. It is contrasted with dauer entry as the alternative developmental outcome.
A quiescent developmental state in which dauer larvae maintain arrested progression. It is a defining feature of dauer diapause and supports long-term survival.
The inactive cellular state maintained by precursor cells during dauer diapause. It reflects developmental arrest and contributes to the persistence of dauer larvae.
The receptor component of the IIS pathway, referred to as DAF-2/insulin receptor in the text. It is the upstream signaling element whose depletion in the somatic gonad promotes dauer entry.
The C. elegans insulin receptor homolog and a central regulator of IIS. Its depletion in the somatic gonad is used experimentally to reveal the role of that tissue in dauer regulation.
A signal transducer within the IIS pathway. It functions downstream of the insulin receptor and contributes to the signaling cascade controlling dauer versus reproductive development.

A transcription factor downstream of IIS that participates in the developmental decision between reproductive growth and dauer entry. It is part of the canonical signaling axis described in the paper.
An experimental intervention used to remove germline precursors. It is employed to test whether the germ line is required for dauer entry under altered insulin signaling in the somatic gonad.
A favorable environmental condition described as supporting rapid, continuous larval development toward reproductive adulthood. It contrasts with adverse conditions that promote dauer formation.
An unfavorable environmental context that triggers the alternative developmental pathway leading to dauer diapause. It is the setting in which L1 larvae divert from normal development.

An environmental context in which C. elegans larvae develop rapidly and continuously through larval stages to reproductive adulthood. It is associated with normal developmental progression rather than dauer entry.
Model organism used to study hormesis, aging, stress resistance, and life extension. It serves as the experimental subject in which IIS-pathway genes and hormetic responses are examined.

A stress-related biological process in which low-level stress exposure induces adaptive responses such as increased stress resistance and extended survival. In this text, it is the central mechanism being studied in relation to aging.
The biological process of functional decline over time, used here as the major context in which hormesis, stress resistance, and lifespan extension are investigated.
An adaptive biological process reflecting enhanced ability to withstand stress. The text distinguishes intrinsic and induced stress resistance and links induced stress resistance to hormesis.
A lifespan-related endpoint indicating increased survival duration. It is described as a consequence of hormesis and is closely related to life extension in the study context.
An outcome representing increased lifespan brought about by hormetic manipulation. It is used as a key endpoint to assess genetic requirements in Caenorhabditis elegans.
The ability to tolerate elevated temperature stress. The text indicates that hormesis can induce thermotolerance and that some genes are required for its full induction.

A conserved signaling pathway implicated in dauer formation, insulin-like signaling, and aging regulation. The text identifies it as having well-established roles in aging and in hormesis-related stress responses.
A gene in the IIS pathway that is required for hormetically induced life extension. It is one of the genetic factors linking hormesis to aging-related outcomes.

A gene in the IIS pathway that blocks hormetically induced life extension when mutated and is required for full induction of thermotolerance. It appears to have a distinct role in stress resistance versus lifespan extension.
A gene in the IIS-related genetic network that blocks hormetically induced life extension when mutated. It contributes to the genetic requirements for hormesis-mediated lifespan effects.
A gene in the IIS pathway whose mutation does not block induced life extension or induced thermotolerance under hormetic conditions. It is part of the comparative genetic analysis in the text.

A gene in the IIS pathway whose mutation does not block induced life extension or induced thermotolerance, although mutants may be unusually sensitive to hormetic conditions. It is relevant to differential genetic sensitivity.
A gene in the IIS pathway whose mutation does not block induced life extension or induced thermotolerance in the hormesis context. It is included among genes tested for functional requirement.
Baseline stress resistance present in the organism independent of hormetic induction. The text contrasts it with induced stress resistance in the study of aging.
Stress resistance that is increased by hormetic manipulation. It is one of the principal adaptive responses discussed in relation to aging and survival.
A lifespan extension phenotype specifically caused by hormesis. The text uses this endpoint to assess whether mutations in IIS-pathway genes block the hormetic response.
Thermotolerance induced by hormetic conditions. The text evaluates whether specific genes are required for its full induction.
The nematode model organism studied in the paper as the primary subject for investigating insulin/IGF-1 signaling, dauer formation, lifespan extension, and healthspan-related aging mechanisms.

A conserved signaling pathway in C. elegans that regulates lifespan, development, dauer entry, and aging-related phenotypes; reduced activity is central to the paper's discussion of longevity and healthspan.
A lowered insulin/IGF-1 signaling state (rIIS) that is associated with lifespan extension and altered aging-related biology in C. elegans and potentially other species.
The insulin/IGF-1 receptor gene in C. elegans; mutations in daf-2 are described as capable of doubling lifespan and are a key genetic perturbation in the IIS pathway.
A diapause-like quiescent larval developmental state in C. elegans that is regulated by IIS and supports survival under harsh environmental conditions through physiological adaptation.
A developmental arrest state referenced as the broader category for dauer, characterized by quiescence and survival adaptation under unfavorable conditions.
The larval developmental form associated with dauer, marked by low activity and survival-oriented physiology.
Adverse environmental conditions that dauer enables C. elegans to endure; serves as the ecological context for the survival advantage of dauer-associated biology.
Structural developmental changes associated with dauer that contribute to survival in harsh environments.
Enhanced repair capacity described as part of dauer-associated survival mechanisms and potentially relevant to reduced IIS-mediated longevity.
A reduced metabolic state associated with dauer and survival under stress, contributing to the organism's ability to endure unfavorable conditions.
The primary longevity outcome discussed in the paper, observed when IIS is reduced or when daf-2 and related pathway genes are mutated.
An aging-related endpoint referring to the quality of healthy life, discussed as a measure of whether reduced IIS improves health rather than only extending lifespan.
A broader aging outcome concerned with maintaining function and health during aging, used here as the conceptual goal for evaluating rIIS effects.
Mechanistic processes that increase lifespan; the paper suggests these may differ between dauer-related and dauer-independent programs under reduced IIS.
Processes associated with dauer biology that may contribute to lifespan extension and possibly health-related parameters under reduced IIS.
Processes that extend lifespan under reduced IIS without relying on dauer-associated mechanisms, highlighted as genetically distinguishable from dauer-related programs.
Additional genetic components of the insulin/IGF-1 signaling pathway whose mutations can influence lifespan in C. elegans.
A higher organism population mentioned as a potential translational context for conserved reduced IIS effects and healthy aging relevance.
The nematode model organism discussed in the review, serving as the biological subject in which ascaroside signaling, development, behavior, and metabolic regulation are examined.

A prominent group of small-molecule signaling compounds in C. elegans that mediate developmental and behavioral phenotypes, including dauer regulation and social/sex-specific behaviors; their activity depends on chemical structure, concentration, and combinations.
The sugar scaffold forming the core of ascaroside chemical structures, linked to fatty acid-like side chains and additional metabolic decorations.
Variable-length lipid-like side chains attached to ascarylose in ascarosides, contributing to structural diversity and altered signaling activity.
Primary metabolites that provide building blocks for additional ascaroside decorations, contributing to chemical diversity and functional specificity.
A primary metabolite mentioned as a source of building blocks used to decorate ascarosides, contributing to structural complexity.
A type of chemosensory head neuron involved in sensing ascarosides and mediating downstream behavioral responses.
A type of chemosensory head neuron that detects ascarosides and participates in signaling pathways controlling developmental and behavioral outputs.
A type of chemosensory head neuron implicated in ascaroside perception and associated behavioral regulation.
Male-specific chemosensory neurons that sense ascarosides and contribute to sex-specific behavioral responses.
A diverse family of receptors that mediate ascaroside perception upstream of conserved intracellular signaling pathways.
A conserved signal transduction pathway acting downstream of ascaroside receptors and involved in regulating developmental and behavioral responses.
A conserved signaling pathway implicated downstream of ascaroside perception in controlling developmental and behavioral phenotypes.

entity_name: PEROXISOMAL Β-OXIDATION OF LONG-CHAIN FATTY ACIDS
description: A metabolic pathway contributing to ascaroside biosynthesis through processing of long-chain fatty acids in peroxisomes.
A primary metabolic pathway that feeds into ascaroside biosynthesis and helps generate structural components or precursors.
A developmental endpoint controlled by ascaroside signaling, reflecting entry into and recovery from the dauer larval stage.
A sex-specific behavioral endpoint regulated by ascarosides, reflecting attraction of males through chemical signaling.
A sex-specific behavioral endpoint influenced by ascarosides, representing avoidance behavior in hermaphrodites.
A behavioral/neural adaptation endpoint modulated by ascaroside signaling, indicating changes in odor response.
A social behavior endpoint controlled by ascarosides, involving group formation or clustering behavior.
A contextual factor affecting ascaroside biosynthesis and signaling, reflecting developmental timing and life-history state in C. elegans.
A biological context that modifies ascaroside biosynthesis and contributes to sex-specific signaling outputs.
An environmental context influencing ascaroside biosynthesis and thereby altering signaling output according to nutritional state.
Broader external conditions that affect ascaroside biosynthesis and encode environmental information into signaling.

A C. elegans experimental population lacking functional C53A5.6/RIKE-1. These animals are the main subject group in which proteotoxic stress, autophagy dysregulation, and epithelial defects are examined.

The nematode model organism used to study conserved mechanisms of proteostasis, autophagy, and epithelial integrity. It provides the biological context for the reported molecular and cellular phenotypes.

A persistent cellular stress state caused by accumulation or misfolding of proteins. In this study it is the upstream perturbation that triggers MTOR sequestration, autophagy overactivation, and epithelial disruption.

entity_name: LOSS OF THE RING AND KELCH REPEAT-CONTAINING PROTEIN C53A5.6/RIKE-1
description: A genetic loss-of-function condition affecting the RING and Kelch repeat-containing protein C53A5.6/RIKE-1. It acts as the initiating perturbation that induces sustained proteotoxic stress and downstream autophagy-related defects.
A RING and Kelch repeat-containing protein implicated in proteostasis maintenance. Its deficiency is central to the observed proteotoxic stress, MTOR sequestration, and epithelial integrity defects.

The C. elegans MTOR-containing complex that is sequestered/aggregated under proteotoxic stress. It is a key regulator of autophagy and is functionally linked to the balance between basal and overactivated autophagy.

An evolutionarily conserved lysosome-dependent degradation pathway that clears intracellular components. In this study, its overactivation is cytotoxic and contributes to epithelial integrity defects.

An excessive autophagic state beyond basal homeostatic levels. It is induced by proteotoxic stress and is associated with cytotoxic effects, endosomal degradation, and epithelial morphogenesis defects.
The structural and functional maintenance of epithelial tissue organization. It is impaired by proteotoxic stress and autophagy overactivation in C53A5.6/RIKE-1-deficient animals.
An autophagy-inhibitory intervention that prevents autophagosome biogenesis. It reduces excessive endosomal degradation and helps restore intestinal morphology in the deficient animals.
An elevated degradative process involving endosomal compartments. It is downstream of autophagy overactivation and contributes to membrane component mislocalization and tissue defects.
Abnormal redistribution of membrane components within intestinal epithelial cells. It is a pathological phenotype mitigated by blocking autophagosome formation.
The structural organization of the intestinal lumen. It is disrupted by C53A5.6/RIKE-1 deficiency and restored when autophagosome formation is blocked.

Suppression of autophagic activity used experimentally to test whether autophagy drives the observed defects. It does not alter LET-363/MTOR aggregation but reduces downstream degradative and morphological abnormalities.
The aggregation/sequestration state of the LET-363/MTOR complex. It reflects altered MTOR localization under proteotoxic stress and is relieved by improving proteostasis.
A functional state in which C53A5.6/RIKE-1 activity is impaired. It is associated with MTOR aggregation and autophagy dysregulation.
A conserved insulin/IGF1 signaling pathway in C. elegans that regulates proteostasis capacity. Its reduction improves proteostasis and suppresses downstream autophagy-related pathology.
The cellular capacity to maintain protein homeostasis through folding, clearance, and quality control. Enhancing this capacity reduces MTOR aggregation and autophagy overactivation.
Abnormal trafficking of endosomal cargo and membranes. It is reversed when proteostasis is improved and autophagy overactivation is alleviated.
Defects in epithelial tissue shaping and organization. They occur in C53A5.6/RIKE-1-deficient animals and are rescued by reducing DAF-2 signaling.
The normal homeostatic level of autophagic activity. The study concludes that C53A5.6/RIKE-1-mediated proteostasis is required to maintain this level.
The tissue-level endpoint reflecting proper epithelial structure and function. It is maintained by C53A5.6/RIKE-1-mediated proteostasis and disrupted by autophagy overactivation.

A conserved signaling family of transforming growth factor beta molecules that regulates reproductive biology across multiple organisms. In this text it is the central molecular system discussed, with roles in germ-cell behavior, developmental patterning, and reproductive tract function.

Members of the TGF-β signaling family described as functional regulators of reproductive processes. They are implicated in balancing germ-cell proliferation and differentiation, maintaining stem-cell identity, and controlling developmental programs in model organisms.

Secreted signaling molecules within the TGF-β family that act as upstream effectors in reproductive development. The text highlights their roles in primordial germ-cell development, sexual differentiation, and gonadal cell development.

Cell-surface receptors that mediate TGF-β family signaling in reproductive tissues and developmental contexts. They are discussed as key components of the signaling pathway governing germ-cell and gonadal development.
The expansion of germ-cell populations, described here as a process balanced by TGF-β-related proteins. It is a core reproductive developmental process influencing fertility and tissue homeostasis.
The maturation of germ cells into specialized reproductive cell types. The text identifies this process as being regulated in balance with proliferation by TGF-β-related proteins.
A developmental decision in Caenorhabditis elegans involving entry into and exit from the dauer stage. The text notes that TGF-β-related proteins influence this process in the nematode model.
The maintenance of stem-like characteristics in germ stem cells. In Drosophila melanogaster, TGF-β-related proteins are described as maintaining this identity, supporting reproductive tissue renewal.
A developmental patterning process in Drosophila melanogaster affecting eggshell formation and structure. The text attributes regulation of this process to TGF-β-related proteins.
The developmental program that generates primordial germ cells. The review identifies this as a major target of TGF-β family ligands and receptors in reproductive development.
The process by which reproductive tissues and organisms develop male or female characteristics. The text states that TGF-β family signaling contributes to this developmental pathway.
Development of cells within the gonads, including processes shaping reproductive organ formation and function. It is described as being influenced by TGF-β family ligands and receptors.
Development of the testis during embryogenesis. The text indicates that mutant mouse studies revealed a contribution of TGF-β family signaling to this process.
Developmental maturation of the testis after birth. The review notes that TGF-β family signaling contributes to this process in mutant mouse studies.
Development of the ovary across embryonic and postnatal stages. The text identifies TGF-β family signaling as contributing to this reproductive developmental process.
The physiological state of proper female reproductive activity and fertility. Human studies in the review highlight the importance of the TGF-β family for maintaining this endpoint.
A reproductive physiological state in which the TGF-β family is described as important for normal female reproductive function. It is presented as a clinically relevant endpoint in human studies.
Disease conditions affecting the female reproductive system. The review states that human studies highlight the importance of the TGF-β family in relation to these pathologies.
A nematode model organism used to study conserved reproductive and developmental signaling. In this text it serves as a species context for TGF-β-related regulation of germ-cell and dauer processes.
A fruit fly model organism used to investigate conserved reproductive developmental pathways. The text uses it to describe TGF-β-related control of germ stem-cell identity and eggshell patterning.
Genetically engineered mouse models used to study reproductive development and signaling pathways. The review cites these models as a major source of evidence for TGF-β family functions.

Mouse-based experimental studies using mutant animals to assess gene function in reproductive development. These studies are described as revealing the contribution of TGF-β family signaling to testis and ovarian development.

Clinical or observational studies in humans used to assess the relevance of TGF-β family signaling to reproductive function. The text uses these studies to support the importance of the pathway in pregnancy and gynecologic disease.

A quiescent larval population of C. elegans used as the biological model in this study. These larvae undergo dauer development in response to adverse environmental cues and are used to examine maintenance of multipotency and adult cell fate regulation during quiescence.

Stem-cell population in the C. elegans epidermis, specifically seam cells, that retains developmental plasticity during dauer. They are the cellular context in which daf-16/FOXO prevents premature adult differentiation.

Epidermal stem cells in C. elegans that serve as the direct cellular target of dauer-associated fate regulation. Their differentiation state is used to assess whether adult cell fate is prematurely adopted.

A stress-resistant, quiescent larval developmental state in C. elegans induced by adverse environmental cues. It provides the developmental setting in which stem/progenitor cells maintain or re-establish multipotency and where daf-16/FOXO activity is examined.
Environmental conditions that trigger entry into dauer. These cues define the context for the quiescent larval stage and the associated stress-resistant developmental program.

The single FOXO ortholog in C. elegans, functioning as a transcription factor that promotes dauer entry, quiescence, stress resistance, and maintenance of multipotency. It also promotes lin-41 expression and blocks premature adult cell fate during dauer.

A conserved family of transcription factors implicated in promoting quiescence and stem cell maintenance. In this paper, daf-16 is the C. elegans FOXO ortholog and is central to the regulatory mechanism studied.

An RNA-binding protein encoded by a heterochronic gene in C. elegans, orthologous to mammalian LIN41/TRIM71. It opposes adult cell fate by inhibiting lin-29 translation and is promoted by daf-16 during dauer.
A conserved zinc finger transcription factor in the heterochronic gene network. It directly activates col-19 transcription and promotes adult cell fate in non-dauer development.

The mammalian orthologous protein family corresponding to C. elegans lin-41. It is referenced to highlight evolutionary conservation of the RNA-binding factor involved in developmental timing and cell fate control.
Adult-enriched collagen genes misexpressed in dauer larvae lacking daf-16. Their expression serves as a molecular indicator of inappropriate adult differentiation during dauer.
A collagen gene whose transcription is directly activated by lin-29 and used as a marker of adult cell fate. Its promoter activity is monitored with col-19p::gfp.

A promoter-reporter construct used as an adult cell fate marker to monitor col-19 expression during dauer and non-dauer development. It provides a readout for premature or normal adult differentiation.

The differentiated developmental state characteristic of adult epidermal identity in C. elegans. The study evaluates whether this fate is prematurely adopted during dauer and how it is regulated by daf-16, lin-41, and lin-29.

The ability of stem and progenitor cells to generate multiple cell types during quiescence. In dauer larvae, maintenance or re-establishment of multipotency is linked to normal developmental recovery after dauer.
A long-term non-division state associated with stem cell maintenance and multipotency. FOXO/daf-16 promotes this process and it forms the physiological context for dauer development.
The preservation of stem-cell identity and functional capacity during non-division or quiescence. FOXO factors are described as promoting this process in the abstract.
The developmental transition into the dauer larval stage in response to adverse environmental cues. daf-16 promotes this process as part of the stress-resistant developmental program.
A physiological property of dauer larvae associated with survival under adverse environmental conditions. daf-16 promotes this stress-resistant state.
The heterochronic developmental program controlling timing and acquisition of adult epidermal characteristics. It involves lin-41, lin-29, and col-19 expression and is altered during dauer.

A developmental timing network that regulates the timing of adult cell fate and col-19p::gfp expression. lin-41 and lin-29 are key components, and daf-16 is proposed to act as a heterochronic gene in dauer.
The protein synthesis process for lin-29 that is inhibited by lin-41 in non-dauer development. This translational control is central to repression of adult cell fate.
Transcriptional activation of the col-19 gene, which is a hallmark of adult cell fate. It is directly promoted by lin-29.

The nematode model organism discussed as the subject in which dauer diapause is regulated. It serves as the experimental population for studying developmental plasticity, signaling pathways, and tissue-specific control of dauer formation.

A diapause developmental program in Caenorhabditis elegans triggered by unfavorable environmental conditions. It represents a major developmental switch involving altered developmental timing, tissue remodeling, and dauer-specific trait acquisition.

entity_name: ENVIRONMENT IS NOT SUITABLE FOR DEVELOPMENT
description: The environmental condition that triggers entry into dauer diapause. It functions as the external context sensed by C. elegans to initiate the dauer developmental decision.
The developmental timing mechanism that must be tightly controlled during the dauer decision. It is implicated in coordinating the detour from normal development toward diapause.

A broad structural and functional reorganization of tissues associated with dauer entry and dauer-specific trait acquisition. It reflects the organism-wide developmental reprogramming required for diapause.
The regulatory pathways that govern the dauer development decision. They integrate environmental cues and coordinate downstream transcriptional and tissue-specific responses.
The developmental choice between normal development and dauer diapause. It is controlled by signaling pathways, transcriptional regulation, and environmental sensing.
The anatomical sites in which dauer-regulatory pathways function to enable acquisition of dauer-specific traits. The review emphasizes tissue-specific contributions to the dauer program.
Phenotypic and functional characteristics acquired during dauer formation. These traits are the downstream developmental outputs of the dauer program.
Inter-pathway communication among dauer-regulatory signaling pathways. It contributes to integrated control and feedback regulation of the dauer program.
Regulatory feedback mechanisms operating among dauer-related signaling pathways. They help stabilize and refine the dauer developmental decision.
Gene-expression control processes governing the dauer program. It is the central focus of the review and contributes to spatiotemporal control of dauer development.
The coordinated developmental program underlying dauer entry, maintenance, and associated trait acquisition. It integrates environmental sensing, signaling, and transcriptional regulation.
The capacity of the organism to alter developmental trajectories in response to environmental conditions. Dauer formation is presented as a model for understanding this property.
The regulatory processes by which the organism commits to one developmental fate over another. In this text, they are described as robustly controlled and capable of all-or-nothing responses.
The binary developmental outcome emphasized as a feature of dauer decision control. It reflects robust regulation of developmental fate choice.
Relevant disease or disorder states for which the dauer developmental decision is proposed as a simplified model. The text frames dauer biology as informative for understanding abnormal development.
An experimental degron-based intervention system listed in the abbreviations. It is used to conditionally degrade target proteins in mechanistic studies.
A signaling molecule listed among dauer-related abbreviations. It is relevant to dauer regulation and developmental decision-making in C. elegans.
A dauer phenotype indicating constitutive formation of dauer larvae. It represents a mutant or regulatory outcome relevant to dauer pathway analysis.
A dauer phenotype indicating defective ability to form dauer larvae. It is a functional outcome used to characterize dauer pathway perturbations.
A specific tissue/cell population listed in the abbreviations. It is relevant as a tissue context potentially involved in dauer-related developmental regulation.
An extracellular matrix state listed in the abbreviations. It represents a localized molecular/structural feature potentially involved in tissue remodeling during dauer.
A receptor family listed in the abbreviations and implicated in signaling pathways governing dauer development. They function as upstream sensory or signaling components.
A conserved signaling pathway listed in the abbreviations and implicated in dauer regulation. It is one of the core pathways governing the dauer developmental decision.
Peptide ligands listed in the abbreviations that participate in insulin/IGF-1 signaling. They are relevant upstream molecular signals in dauer regulation.
A receptor domain listed in the abbreviations. It is a molecular feature relevant to ligand recognition in signaling components involved in dauer regulation.
A developmental stage listed in the abbreviations, referring to the L4 stage after dauer. It is relevant as a post-dauer developmental population stratum.
A conserved signaling pathway listed in the abbreviations and implicated in dauer regulation. It contributes to the network of pathways controlling dauer development.
The reference genetic background listed in the abbreviations. It serves as the baseline population for comparing dauer-related phenotypes and pathway function.

A nematode model organism used here as the biological subject in which germline proliferation and insulin/IGF-like signaling are studied. It serves as the experimental population for understanding developmental and physiological control of cell proliferation.

The process of germ cell division and expansion in the reproductive lineage of C. elegans. It is the central biological process discussed, regulated by insulin/IGF-like signaling and linked to adult stem/progenitor population size and fecundity.

A conserved signaling pathway implicated in developmental and physiological regulation of cell proliferation. In this text, it is the key upstream process controlling germline proliferation in C. elegans, with stage- and tissue-specific effects.
The developmental program that gives rise to the germline in C. elegans. It provides the context in which insulin/IGF-like signaling influences proliferation and reproductive capacity.
The resulting adult germline stem/progenitor cell pool whose proper generation depends on insulin pathway activity. It is a functional developmental endpoint tied to reproductive fitness.
Reproductive output or fertility of the organism. In this context, optimal fecundity is an outcome supported by proper insulin-dependent germline proliferation.
The larval developmental window during which insulin signaling acts on germline proliferation. This stage-specific context distinguishes the reproductive state from dauer larval stages.

An alternative larval developmental state in C. elegans that is contrasted with reproductive larval stages. The insulin pathway role in germline proliferation is described as restricted to reproductive rather than dauer stages.
A specific cell-cycle phase mentioned as the point at which insulin signaling impinges during germline proliferation. It indicates a mechanistic cell-cycle control aspect of the pathway's action.
Putative signaling molecules that act as ligands in the insulin pathway. Two specific ligands are noted as especially important for the germline role and as having tissue-specific signaling behavior.
A subset of insulin-like ligands whose regulation and tissue-specific responses are highlighted as future research targets. They are implicated in the specificity of germline signaling responses.
Differential signaling responses that vary by tissue context. The text emphasizes that insulin signaling elicits tissue-specific effects, especially in relation to germline proliferation.

A nematode model organism discussed as the subject whose development responds to nutrient limitation. It is the biological system in which nutrient sensing, developmental arrest, and progression are being considered.

A low-nutrient environmental condition that acts as the triggering exposure/context for altered developmental responses in C. elegans. It is the central scenario driving arrest, slowed development, and survival strategies.
The process of advancing through developmental stages in C. elegans. It is regulated by nutrient sensing pathways and is altered under nutrient limitation.
A developmental endpoint in which larvae stop progressing, serving as a survival strategy under nutrient limitation. It reflects a major phenotypic response to adverse nutritional conditions.
A measurable slowing of developmental progression under nutrient limitation. It represents an adaptive outcome that allows survival when nutrients are scarce.

A developmental program in C. elegans that produces the dauer larval stage as a long-term survival strategy. It is induced in response to nutrient limitation and is part of developmental decision-making.
A nutrient-sensing signaling component/pathway mentioned as part of the integrated response to nutrient information. It helps regulate developmental progression in C. elegans.
A signaling molecule/pathway component involved in integrating nutrient information. It participates in signaling pathways that regulate developmental progression in response to nutrient status.
The intracellular communication networks that integrate nutrient-sensing inputs and control developmental decisions. In the abstract, these pathways include TOR and insulin signaling.

The biological process by which essential nutrient availability is detected and translated into developmental responses. It is the upstream mechanism enabling adaptive developmental progression decisions.

The regulatory process by which C. elegans selects among developmental outcomes such as arrest, slowed growth, or dauer formation. These decisions are shaped by nutrient information and signaling integration.

Adaptive biological responses used to persist under nutrient limitation, including larval arrest, decreased developmental rate, and dauer formation. They represent functional outcomes of nutrient-responsive developmental control.
